definition.name: Church Communication Platform
definition.overview:
A **Church Communication Platform** is an organization-side messaging application through which a church (or a similar faith organization) sends managed messages to its own people — members, guests, volunteers, and staff — and handles what comes back.

The defining core is a communication loop with four parts:

```text
Church as sender (its own sending identity)
└── People of the church (identified records: members, guests, volunteers, staff)
    └── Audiences selected from those people (groups / lists)
        └── Composed messages delivered over channels (email, SMS, and optionally voice or app push)
            └── Managed return path (replies, comments, opt-outs handled in the same system)
```

The loop is what makes the Type recognizable. Remove the church's own people as the audience substrate and the product becomes a generic email or SMS marketing tool; remove the sending loop and it becomes a church management system; remove the organization sender and it becomes personal messaging.

Everything else commonly associated with these products — automated follow-up sequences, text keywords, digital connect cards, templates, delivery analytics, church-app push notifications, calling features — is standard capability layered on the loop, not part of what defines it.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**教会沟通平台**是一个组织端消息应用程序，通过它，教会（或类似的信仰组织）向其成员——成员、嘉宾、志愿者和员工——发送管理消息，并处理回复。

定义的核心是一个包含四个部分的通信循环：

```text
教会作为发送者（其自身的发送身份）
└── 教会的人员（已识别记录：成员、嘉宾、志愿者、员工）
    └── 从这些人员中选择的受众（组/列表）
        └── 通过渠道投递的已编撰消息（电子邮件、短信，以及可选语音或应用推送）
            └── 管理的返回路径（回复、评论、退订在同一系统中处理）
```

这个循环使得该类型可识别。移除教会自己的人员作为受众基础，产品就变成通用的电子邮件或短信营销工具；移除发送循环，它就变成教会管理系统；移除组织发送者，它就变成个人消息传递。

其他通常与这些产品相关的功能——自动跟进序列、文本关键词、数字连接卡、模板、投递分析、教会应用推送通知、呼叫功能——是叠加在循环上的标准能力，而不是定义它的部分。
definition.dc:
**Organization-operated sending identity.** The church itself is the sender. The application operates a message identity belonging to the organization — a phone number and/or email address — so that messages come from the church, not from a staff member's personal phone or inbox. This is what allows several staff and volunteers to send on behalf of one church, and what keeps ministry communication separate from personal devices.

**People-based audience.** Recipients are identified individuals held as people records — members, regular attenders, first-time guests, volunteers, staff — either stored in the platform or synchronized from a church management system. This is the structural difference from marketing tools built on anonymous subscriber lists: the audience is the church's own community, with names, households, group memberships, and roles attached to the records.

**Audiences as groups or lists.** People are organized into named audiences — small groups, serving teams, ministries, age groups, guest lists — and messages are addressed to one or more of these audiences, to roles, or to the entire church. The audience container is the everyday unit of targeting; staff rarely message "everyone" without meaning a specific segment.

**Composed outbound message.** A message is composed in the application, addressed to an audience, and delivered over one or more channels. Email and SMS text messaging form the base channel pair across the researched products; voice broadcast, video messages, and app push notifications appear as additional channels in some products. Messages can be sent immediately or scheduled for later.

**Managed return path.** The loop closes inside the same system. Recipient replies arrive in an inbox and are answered as one-to-one conversations; comments may be attached to a message; opt-out requests (such as replying STOP, or unsubscribing from email) are recorded and honored so the person stops receiving that channel. The return path is what makes this pastoral communication rather than one-way broadcasting.
definition.dc_zh:
**组织运营的发送身份。** 教会本身是发送者。应用程序运营一个属于组织的消息身份——一个电话号码和/或电子邮件地址——因此消息来自教会，而不是来自员工的个人手机或收件箱。这允许多名员工和志愿者代表一个教会发送消息，并将事工通信与个人设备保持分离。

**基于人员的受众。** 收件人是作为人员记录被识别的个体——成员、常客、首次访客、志愿者、员工——存储在平台中或从教会管理系统中同步。这是与基于匿名订阅列表的营销工具的结构差异：受众是教会自己的社区，记录中附加了姓名、家庭、小组成员身份和角色。

**受众作为群组或列表。** 人被组织成命名的受众——小组、服务团队、事工、年龄组、访客列表——消息被发送给一个或多个这些受众、角色或整个教会。受众容器是定向的日常单位；员工很少发送消息给“所有人”而不指定特定细分。

**编写出站消息。** 消息在应用中编写，针对受众，并通过一个或多个渠道交付。
definition.rules:
### Consent governs the audience

People are messaged because they opted in — by joining, by texting a keyword, by submitting a connect card — or because they are part of the church's community. Opt-out is equally structural: a STOP reply or unsubscribe removes the person from that channel, and the system honors it on subsequent sends. Text messaging in particular is treated as consent-sensitive, and vendors document opt-in and opt-out handling as first-class operations.

### Channels behave differently

Email and SMS are not interchangeable in behavior. SMS delivery is fragile in ways email is not — mobile carriers filter messages, which is why vendors publish deliverability best practices and why sender-identity choices (the kind of phone number used) matter. Email offers richer formatting and open/click tracking, but vendors themselves caution that opens and clicks are not a reliable delivery status. A staff member learns to pick the channel to fit the message and the moment.

### Replies are conversations, not group chats

When a message goes to two hundred people and several reply, each reply is a separate one-to-one conversation with that person in the church's inbox — not a group thread among recipients. This preserves pastoral privacy and is a deliberate contrast with group-messaging products.

### Sending is a permission, not a given

Not every account user can message everyone. Products restrict who may send (account-level permissions) and often scope sending rights to the groups a user administers. This reflects real church governance: communication on behalf of the congregation is delegated deliberately.

### The audience must stay current

Messages are only as good as the list behind them. Sync with a church management system, bounce cleanup, and profile-change tracking exist because the audience changes constantly; sending to a stale list is the failure mode these mechanisms prevent.

### Inbound and outbound are not symmetric

Replies from people typically do not consume the same resources as outbound sends in metered products, and delivery indicators (such as a sent confirmation) are the sender's window into whether a message reached its recipient.
definition.rules_zh:
### 同意管理受众

人们被发送消息是因为他们选择加入——通过加入、通过发送文本关键词、通过提交连接卡——或者因为他们是教会社区的一部分。退订同样具有结构性：STOP回复或取消订阅会将该人从该渠道移除，系统在后续发送时遵守这一点。短信尤其被视为同意敏感，供应商将加入和退订处理记录为一流操作。

### 渠道行为不同

电子邮件和短信在行为上不可互换。短信的投递方式脆弱，电子邮件则不然——移动运营商过滤消息，这就是为什么供应商发布可投递性最佳实践，以及为什么发送者身份选择（使用的电话号码类型）很重要。电子邮件提供更丰富的格式和打开/点击跟踪，但供应商自己警告说，打开和点击不是可靠的投递状态。员工学会选择渠道以适应消息和时刻。

### 回复是对话，而不是群聊

当消息发送给两百人且有几人回复时，每个回复都是在教会收件箱中与该人的一对一对话，而不是收件人之间的群聊。这保留了牧养隐私，并与群组消息产品形成刻意对比。

### 发送是一种权限，而不是必然

并非每个账户用户都可以向所有人发送消息。产品限制谁可以发送（账户级权限），并且通常将发送权限限定于用户管理的组。这反映了真实的教会治理：代表会众的沟通是刻意委派的。

### 受众必须保持最新

消息的质量取决于背后的列表。与教会管理系统同步、弹回清理和资料更新是维护的关键。

definition.name: Church Management System / ChMS
definition.overview:
A **Church Management System (ChMS)** is a congregation's central record system: it holds identified people — organized into households or families — as its core records, attaches their participation over time (attendance, group involvement, giving history, serving) to those records, and is operated by the church's own staff and lay leaders as an administrative system of record for ministry.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
Congregation people records (individuals + households)
└── Participation records over time, attached to the person
    └── Church-side administration (staff/leaders govern the records;
        members are the subjects — and partial self-servers — of the records)
```

Everything else commonly associated with church software — children's check-in kiosks, giving tools, texting, church apps, volunteer scheduling, websites — is standard capability layered around that record core, not what makes the product a ChMS. A parish census register or a 1990s office membership database satisfies the core without any of the modern machinery; conversely, a product without people records is not a ChMS no matter how many church features it has.

The record core is also why the surrounding church-software market is organized the way it is: giving platforms, communication platforms, scheduling specialists, and worship planners all exist beside the ChMS, integrate with it, or ship as its modules. A ChMS can lack any one of those modules and remain a ChMS; it cannot lack the record core.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**教会管理系统（ChMS）** 是会众的中央记录系统：它保存已识别的人员——按家庭或家族组织——作为其核心记录，将他们随时间变化的参与（出席、小组参与、奉献历史、服务）附加到这些记录上，并由教会自己的工作人员和世俗领袖作为事工的行政记录系统来操作。

定义的核心故意设计得很小：

```text
会众人员记录（个人 + 家庭）
└── 随时间变化的参与记录，附加到个人
    └── 教会端行政管理（工作人员/领袖管理记录；
        成员是记录的主体——也是部分自助服务者——）
```

其他通常与教会软件相关的一切——儿童签到亭、奉献工具、短信、教会应用、志愿者排班、网站——是围绕该记录核心的标准能力，并不是使产品成为 ChMS 的东西。教区登记簿或 1990 年代的办公室会员数据库在没有任何现代机制的情况下满足了核心要求；相反，一个没有人员记录的产品，无论有多少教会功能，都不是 ChMS。

记录核心也是周围教会软件市场如此组织的原因：奉献平台、通信平台、排班专家和敬拜规划者都与 ChMS 并存、集成或作为其模块发布。一个 ChMS 可以缺少这些模块中的任何一个而仍然是 ChMS；但它不能缺少记录核心。
definition.dc:
**Person record.** The central object: an identified individual with contact details, demographic fields (name, birth date, gender, contact information are typical defaults), and an extensible set of custom fields (custom tabs and typed fields — text, date, dropdown, checkbox, file — are common). The person record is the anchor to which everything else attaches.

**Household / family.** People are grouped into households or families as first-class units. The household matters because church life is largely familial: address and contact info are often held at household level, giving and attendance can be recorded per family, and children belong to a household under their guardians.

**Participation records.** The person's history of engagement, accumulated over time and visible on the profile: attendance at services, events, and groups; membership in groups and teams; contribution history; serving history; notes. This is what distinguishes a ChMS from a static member directory — the record is a *life of involvement*, not just a listing.

**Church-side administration.** The system is governed by the organization: staff and leaders hold permissioned access, sensitive data is visibility-controlled, and members' self-service is scoped by the church. The church owns the data; members are its subjects.
definition.dc_zh:
**人员记录。** 中心对象：一个已识别的个人，具有联系方式、人口统计字段（姓名、出生日期、性别、联系信息是典型默认值），以及一组可扩展的自定义字段（自定义选项卡和类型化字段——文本、日期、下拉列表、复选框、文件——很常见）。人员记录是锚点，所有其他内容都附着其上。

**家庭。** 人员被分组到家庭或家庭中作为一级单位。家庭重要，因为教会生活在很大程度上是家庭式的：地址和联系信息通常在家庭级别持有，奉献和出勤可以按家庭记录，儿童属于监护人下的家庭。

**参与记录。** 个人参与的历史，随时间累积并在个人资料中可见：出席服务、事件和小组；加入小组和团队；奉献历史；服务历史；备注。这是区分ChMS与静态成员目录的关键——记录是*参与生活*，而不仅仅是列表。

**教会管理。** 系统由组织管理：工作人员和领导拥有权限访问，敏感数据受可见性控制，成员自助服务由教会界定。教会拥有数据；成员是其主体。
definition.rules:
### The record core is shared

Every module — giving, check-in, groups, events, communication — writes back to the same person record. This single-profile invariant is the ChMS's central promise: attendance, giving, and group involvement are read together on one profile, and it is why standalone tools in the same market advertise their integration with the ChMS database.

### Members are subjects, not operators

Self-service is real but scoped: members may edit designated fields of their own profile and interact with their own groups, while governance of the data — and of everyone else's — stays with the church. Some products keep children out of member accounts entirely, tracking minors through check-in rather than login.

### Congregant data is sensitive by default

Notes about counseling, health, or prayer requests; membership in recovery or care groups; and children's locations are visibility-controlled structures, not settings afterthoughts. Confidential group membership can be anonymous even to other members; sensitive profile fields can be masked from staff without explicit access; and, in some products, security labels deliberately omit information (such as a child's location) that must not leak to whoever holds the printed label.

### Check-in is a custody protocol

A child's checkout depends on matching security labels or codes, or on verifying that the arriving adult is authorized — even when labels don't match. Room capacity limits and live rosters support the same duty of care.

### Attendance is a pastoral signal

Because participation history accumulates on the person, absence becomes visible: lists of first-time guests, of regulars who stopped attending, of households without contact information. Much of the workflow machinery exists to act on exactly these signals — the records are kept not only for administration but to keep people "from falling through the cracks."

### Contribution records are distinct from collection channels

The ChMS records and attributes gifts; the channels that move money (online forms, text giving, kiosks) may be bundled, but conceptually belong to the giving platform that feeds the record. Statements and pledge tracking flow from the record, not the channel.

### Lifecycle is managed, not assumed

Moving from guest to regular to member to inactive is typically an explicit, tracked progression — via status fields, workflow steps, or milestone records — because follow-up, communication eligibility, and directory visibility often depend on it. Exact status vocabularies vary by product and by denomination.
definition.rules_zh:
### 记录核心是共享的

每个模块——奉献、签到、小组、活动、通信——都写回同一个人员记录。这个单一档案不变性是 ChMS 的核心承诺：出席、奉献和小组参与在同一个档案上一起查看，这也是同一市场中的独立工具宣传其与 ChMS 数据库集成的原因。

### 成员是主体，不是操作者

自助服务是真实的但有范围限制：成员可以编辑自己档案的指定字段并与其自己的小组互动，而数据的治理——以及其他所有人的数据——由教会掌握。一些产品将儿童完全排除在成员账户之外，通过签到而非登录来跟踪未成年人。

### 会众数据默认敏感

关于咨询、健康或祈祷请求的备注；康复或关怀小组的成员资格；以及儿童位置是可见性控制的结构，而不是事后设置。机密小组成员资格即使对其他成员也可以是匿名的；敏感档案字段可以对没有明确访问权限的工作人员隐藏；在一些产品中，安全标签故意省略信息（如儿童位置），这些信息不得泄露给持有打印标签的任何人。

### 签到是监护协议

儿童的签出取决于匹配安全标签或代码，或者验证到达的成年人是否被授权——即使标签不匹配。房间容量限制和实时名册支持相同的照护职责。

### 出席是牧养信号

因为参与历史累积在个人身上，缺席变得可见：首次访客列表、停止出席的常规成员列表、没有联系信息的家庭列表。许多工作流机制正是为了对这一点采取行动。

definition.name: Church Website Builder
definition.overview:
A **Church Website Builder** is an application a church uses to build and maintain its public website. Its defining core has three parts:

```text
Hosted public website (the church's own domain, operated by the vendor)
└── Church-shaped building blocks (welcome/service info, sermons, events, giving, guest welcome)
    └── Built and maintained by non-technical church staff and volunteers
```

The managed output is not a document or a campaign but a **living public website**: the "front door" people check before visiting, where they find service times and location, watch or listen to messages, see events, give, and take a first step toward visiting. What separates this Type from a generic website builder is that the site is assembled from structures shaped around church life — provided ready-made by the product — rather than composed from generic business widgets, and that it connects into the church's operations (giving, member records, church app).

Everything else commonly bundled with these products — design libraries, podcast feeds, livestream embedding, SEO tooling, prayer walls, AI site drafts, done-for-you build services — is widespread but not what makes the product a church website builder.
definition.overview_zh:
**教堂网站构建器**是一种应用程序，教会用它来构建和维护其公共网站。其定义核心有三个部分：

```text
托管的公共网站（教会自己的域名，由供应商运营）
└── 教堂形状的构建块（欢迎/服务信息、讲道、活动、奉献、访客欢迎）
    └── 由非技术性的教会员工和志愿者构建和维护
```

管理输出不是文档或活动，而是一个**活的公共网站**：人们在访问前检查的“前门”，他们在这里找到服务时间和地点，观看或收听信息，查看活动，奉献，并迈出访问的第一步。将这种**类型**与通用网站构建器区分开来的是，该网站是围绕教会生活形状的结构组装的——由产品提供现成——而不是由通用业务小部件组成，并且它连接到教会的运营（奉献、成员记录、教堂应用）。

与这些产品常见的其他一切——设计库、播客源、直播嵌入、SEO工具、祈祷墙、AI网站草案、为您构建的服务——很普遍，但不是使产品成为教堂网站构建器的原因。
definition.dc:
```text
Church (identity: name, branding, locations, service times)
└── Website (hosted, public, under the church's domain)
    ├── Pages → composed of sections/blocks
    ├── Navigation menus
    ├── Design (template/theme + branding applied sitewide)
    └── Church-life objects (sermons, events, giving, guest capture, livestream, staff/ministries)
└── Operators (staff/volunteers with roles and permissions)
└── Connections (giving platform, member records, church app, calendars, social)
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a church website builder:

- **Hosted public website as the managed output.** The deliverable is a complete, publicly addressable website under the church's own domain. Hosting, security certificates, and uptime are operated by the vendor — the church never touches a server. Without this, the product is an authoring tool, not a website builder.
- **Church-shaped site structure.** The building blocks are pre-built around church life: a welcome/service-times-and-location core, a sermon/message library with podcast distribution, an events calendar, giving, and guest welcome/follow-up. The church fills in its own content rather than assembling these structures from generic widgets. Without this, the product is a generic website builder that a church happens to use.
- **Non-technical church operators.** Building and ongoing maintenance are done by staff and volunteers through template-driven, visual editing — no code. Without this, the product is a web agency service or a developer tool.
definition.dc_zh:
教会（标识：名称、品牌、地点、礼拜时间）
└── 网站（托管式、公开可访问、使用教会自有域名）
    ├── 页面 → 由版块/模块组成
    ├── 导航菜单
    ├── 设计（应用全站的模板/主题 + 品牌元素）
    └── 教会生活对象（讲道、活动、奉献、访客接待、直播、同工/事工）
└── 运营者（具有角色与权限的同工/志愿者）
└── 连接（奉献平台、会员记录、教会应用、日历、社交平台）
definition.rules:
### The site is public; sensitive content needs explicit protection

Everything published is world-readable. Products therefore provide privacy machinery — for example, prayer requests kept out of search results and viewable only to signed-in members, password-protected pages, or private media playlists for internal material. Privacy is a structural concern, not an afterthought, because churches publish both public invitation and intimate community content on the same site.

### Church identity data is single-sourced

Name, address, service times, and branding are entered once and reused across the site. A service-time change is one edit, not a hunt through pages.

### Content objects are single-sourced and multi-surfaced

A sermon published once appears in the sermon hub, the podcast feed, and (where connected) the church app. An event appears on the calendar and in promotion surfaces. The publisher manages the object, not each surface.

### Design is layered over content

Refreshing or changing the design does not require re-entering the site's content; one product makes swapping the entire design a one-click operation. Churches redesign seasonally without rebuilding.

### Time-sensitive content can be given a lifecycle

Some products let announcements and banners be scheduled to appear and expire automatically, so stale content does not linger — a direct answer to the volunteer-maintained reality of church websites.

### The church keeps its domain; the vendor operates the hosting

The public address belongs to the church and can be pointed at the builder (and away from it). Hosting, certificates, and uptime are the vendor's responsibility — churches do not manage servers, backups, or security patches themselves.

### Editors are many and transient; permissions are scoped

Volunteers rotate. Products support multiple simultaneous editors with scoped permissions (one page, one form, one content area) so broad access is not required for narrow jobs.

### Giving is embedded, not owned

Donations initiated on the site are processed by a giving platform (native to the suite or integrated); the website builder provides the placement and the connection, not the payment rails.
definition.rules_zh:
### 网站是公共的；敏感内容需要明确保护

发布的所有内容都是世界可读的。因此，产品提供隐私机制——例如，祈祷请求不显示在搜索结果中，只有登录的成员才能查看，受密码保护的页面，或用于内部材料的私人媒体播放列表。隐私是结构性问题，而不是事后思考，因为教会在同一网站上发布公共邀请和亲密社区内容。

### 教堂身份数据是单一来源的

名称、地址、服务时间和品牌输入一次，在整个网站中重复使用。服务时间的更改是一次编辑，而不是在页面中搜寻。

### 内容对象是单一来源和多表面的

一次发布的讲道出现在讲道中心、播客源中，以及（如果连接）教堂应用中。活动出现在日历和推广表面中。发布者管理对象，而不是每个表面。

### 设计叠加在内容之上

刷新或更改设计不需要重新输入网站内容；一个产品使交换整个设计成为一次点击操作。教会季节性重新设计，而无需重建。

### 时间敏感的内容可以赋予生命周期

一些产品允许公告和横幅被安排自动出现和过期，这样陈旧的内容就不会停留——这是对教会网站由志愿者维护现实的直接回应。

### 教会保留其域名；供应商运营托管

公共地址属于教会，可以指向构建器（也可以指向其他地方）。托管、证书和正常运行时间是供应商的责任——教会自己不管理服务器、备份或安全补丁。

### 编辑者众多且临时；权限是结构化的

definition.name: Committee / Board Management
definition.overview:
A **Committee / Board Management** application — in the market most often called *board management software* or a *board portal* — is the system an organization uses to run its governing bodies: the board of directors or trustees, and the committees that carry out much of the detailed work between board meetings. It keeps the roster of each body and its members, organizes each body's recurring meeting cycle — agenda, distributed meeting materials, the meeting itself, minutes — and preserves the confirmed record of decisions and follow-up actions as the organization's official governance memory.

This is the form the category takes in nonprofits, trade and professional associations, churches, schools, clubs, healthcare and community organizations, and other member-governed bodies. Three conditions of that market shape the software: the members are usually volunteers, not employees; they serve fixed terms and rotate; and an organization typically runs several small bodies in parallel — a board plus a handful of committees — each with its own people, meetings, and records.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
Governed body (board or committee) with an identified member roster carrying roles
└── Meeting as the unit of governance work for that body
    ├── Agenda structuring the meeting
    ├── Meeting materials distributed to the body's members
    │   under member-scoped access
    └── Confirmed governance record — minutes, decisions, actions —
        retained as the body's official account
```

Everything else the category is known for — board books, voting, e-signatures, discussion threads, term tracking, public transparency sites, AI drafting — is standard or optional capability layered on this core. The software exists because the meeting cycle is recurring and formal, the materials are confidential to the body's members, and the record must be authoritative; email threads, shared drives, and generic meeting tools provide none of those guarantees.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**委员会/董事会管理**应用——在市场上通常称为*董事会管理软件*或*董事会门户*——是组织用来运行其治理主体的系统：董事会或受托委员会，以及执行董事会会议间大量细节工作的委员会。它保存每个主体及其成员的名单，组织每个主体的重复会议周期——议程、分发的会议材料、会议本身、会议记录——并保存确认的决策和后续行动记录作为组织的正式治理记忆。

这是该类别在非营利组织、贸易和专业协会、教堂、学校、俱乐部、医疗保健和社区组织以及其他成员治理主体中的形式。该市场的三个条件塑造了软件：成员通常是志愿者，而不是员工；他们服务固定任期并轮换；一个组织通常并行运行几个小型主体——一个董事会加上若干委员会——每个都有自己的人员、会议和记录。

定义性核心故意保持简洁：

```text
治理主体（董事会或委员会）具有明确的成员名单并承载角色
└── 会议作为该主体治理工作的单元
    ├── 议程构建会议
    ├── 会议材料分发给该主体的成员
    │   在成员范围访问控制下
    └── 确认的治理记录——会议记录、决策、行动——
        保留作为该主体的官方记录
```

该类别已知的其他所有功能——董事会手册、投票、电子签名、讨论线程、任期跟踪、公共透明网站、AI起草——都是建立在核心之上的标准或可选能力。软件之所以存在，是因为会议周期是重复和正式的，材料对主体的成员是机密的，记录必须是权威的；电子邮件线程、共享驱动器和通用会议工具都不提供这些保证。
definition.dc:
**Governed body.** The organizing container is the body — the board or a committee — a named governing unit of the organization with its own member roster. Each member is an identified person holding a role on that body (chair, secretary, treasurer, member). The body scopes everything else: who receives its materials, who may vote, whose record this is.

**Meeting.** The unit of governance work is the meeting: a dated, scheduled occasion of a specific body, with attendees, a location or remote link, and a lifecycle that runs from scheduling through materials, conduct, and minutes to confirmation. Meetings recur on a calendar; past meetings accumulate into the body's institutional memory.

**Agenda-structured materials.** The agenda structures the meeting into items, and the meeting materials attach to those items. The assembled set — the *board packet* or *board book* — is distributed to the body's members under member-scoped access: it is addressed to the members of that body, access is controlled per person, and the materials live inside the platform rather than as email attachments.

**Confirmed governance record.** The meeting produces the record: minutes drafted against the agenda, with recorded decisions, motions and votes, and action items (each with an owner and follow-up). Minutes are reviewed and confirmed — typically at the following meeting — and the confirmed record is retained as the body's official account. Past packets, minutes, and policies accumulate into a searchable governance library.
definition.dc_zh:
**治理机构。** 组织容器是机构本身——董事会或委员会——这是组织内拥有自身成员名录的命名治理单元。每位成员都是在该机构中担任角色（主席、秘书、财务、成员）的特定个人。该机构界定一切：谁接收其材料、谁可以投票、这是谁的记录。

**会议。** 治理工作的单元是会议：特定机构的、有日期和日程安排的场合，具有参与者、地点或远程链接，以及从安排日程、分发材料、会议进行、记录纪要到最终确认的生命周期。会议在日历上循环召开；过去的会议逐渐积累成该机构的制度记忆。

**议程结构化材料。** 议程将会议结构化为若干议题，会议材料附属于这些议题。整理好的材料集合——*董事会文件包* 或 *委员会资料册*——按照成员范围控制的访问权限分发给该机构成员：它专为该机构成员准备，访问权限按个人控制，材料存储在平台内部而非作为电子邮件附件。

**确认的治理记录。** 会议产出记录：根据议程起草的会议纪要，记录决议、动议和投票，以及行动项（每项都有负责人和后续跟进）。会议纪要会被审阅并确认——通常在下一次会议上——确认后的记录...
definition.rules:
**Body-scoped isolation.** Membership in one body grants nothing in another. A committee's meetings, documents, decisions, and people are separate from the board's and from other committees'; a person serving on two bodies holds two distinct memberships. This is the structural rule that makes committees safe containers for sensitive work (finance, personnel, fundraising strategy).

**Member-scoped access; materials stay in the platform.** Papers are distributed to the body's members as platform content with per-person access control — not as email attachments. Revoking access removes visibility. The category's founding promise is the retirement of emailed and photocopied board papers.

**Stage gates and the locked record.** Published materials are versioned, never silently overwritten; late changes produce a new version with the original retained. Draft agendas and draft minutes are labeled as such. After confirmation, the minutes are locked — the approved record cannot be quietly changed, and past decisions stay answerable ("what did we decide and why?").

**Controlled visibility of history.** When a new member joins, what they can see of past discussions, tasks, and polls is a deliberate policy — in collaborative products, current documents and meetings are typically visible while older conversations remain private unless explicitly shared. Organizations control how much historical context a transition carries.

**The record outlives the member.** Terms end; the body's record persists. The system is the continuity mechanism for volunteer rotation — this is why minutes, decisions, and the library are retained as an archive rather than as project files.

**Volunteer adoption constrains design.** The member surface must be usable without training, on any device, with accessibility support; complexity concentrates in the administrator workspace. Products compete heavily on this, and it explains why the member experience across the category looks more like a consumer app than enterprise software.
definition.rules_zh:
**主体范围隔离。** 在一个主体中的成员资格不授予另一个主体的任何权利。一个委员会的会议、文件、决策和人员与董事会和其他委员会的分开；在两个主体中服务的人持有两个不同的成员资格。这是使委员会成为敏感工作（财务、人事、筹款策略）安全容器的结构规则。

**成员范围访问；材料留在平台中。** 文件作为平台内容分发给主体的成员，具有按人访问控制——而不是作为电子邮件附件。撤销访问会移除可见性。该类别的创始承诺是淘汰通过电子邮件和影印分发的董事会文件。

**阶段门和锁定记录。** 发布的材料是版本化的，从不被静默覆盖；后期的更改会产生一个新版本，同时保留原版。草稿议程和草稿会议记录被标记为草稿。确认后，会议记录被锁定——批准的记录不能被静默更改，过去的决策保持可追溯（"我们决定了什么以及为什么？"）。

**历史记录的可控可见性。** 当新成员加入时，他们可以看到过去讨论、任务和投票的量是一个有意的策略——在协作产品中，当前文档和会议通常可见，而旧对话保持私密，除非明确共享。组织控制过渡携带多少历史上下文。

**记录比成员更持久。** 任期结束；主体的记录持续存在。系统是志愿者轮换的连续性机制——这就是为什么会议记录、决策和库被保留为存档，而不是项目文件。

**志愿者采纳约束设计。** 成员界面必须在没有培训的情况下可用，在任何设备上，具有可访问性，

definition.name: Congregation Membership Management
definition.overview:
A **Congregation Membership Management** application is the church-side system that maintains the congregation's roll of people: identified individuals, organized into households, each carrying a recorded membership status, administered by the church's own staff and leaders. It answers the most basic administrative question a congregation has — who belongs to us, who is connected but not yet enrolled, who has moved away, who has drifted — and produces the directories, lists, labels, and reports that the rest of church administration runs on.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
Congregation people roll (identified individuals)
└── Recorded membership status per person
    └── Church-side administration of the roll
```

Everything else commonly associated with church software — attendance kiosks, giving tools, group modules, texting, member apps — is standard capability layered around the roll, or belongs to neighboring application types. A parish register, a paper membership roll with letters of transfer, or a 1990s single-desktop office database satisfies the core without any modern machinery.

In the market this type appears in two shapes: as **standalone products and modules** (a free membership database usable entirely on its own; a membership module purchasable separately from a desktop suite; a parish census and family-directory module), and as the **record core inside full church management systems**. What makes it a type of its own is the roll itself — people, households, membership status, and the outputs derived from them — without the operational machinery (check-in stations, giving collection, groups, events) whose presence would make the product a full Church Management System.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**教会会众会员管理**应用程序是教会侧的系统，用于维护会众的名册：识别出的个人，组织到家庭中，每个家庭都记录了会员状态，由教会自身的员工和领袖管理。它回答会众最基本的问题——谁属于我们，谁有联系但尚未正式加入，谁已经搬走，谁已经疏远——并生成教会其他管理工作的目录、名单、标签和报告。

其定义的核心是刻意保持小巧的：

```text
会众人员名册（识别出的个人）
└── 每人记录的会员状态
    └── 教会侧对名册的管理
```

所有其他通常与教会软件相关的东西——签到亭、捐赠工具、小组模块、短信、会员应用——都是围绕名册构建的标准功能，或者属于相邻的应用程序类型。一个教区登记册、一份带有转介信的纸质会员名册，或者一个90年代的单机桌面办公数据库，都能在不使用任何现代技术的情况下满足核心需求。

在市场上，这种类型以两种形式出现：作为**独立产品和模块**（一个完全可以独立使用的免费会员数据库；一个可以从桌面套件中单独购买的会员模块；一个教区人口普查和家庭目录模块），以及作为**完整教会管理系统内部的记录核心**。使其成为独立类型的是名册本身——人员、家庭、会员状态以及从中衍生出的输出——而非运营机制（签到站、捐赠收集、小组、活动），后者的存在会使该产品成为完整的教会管理系统。
definition.dc: **Church-side administration.** Staff and lay leaders hold permissioned access and maintain the roll; members may self-edit scoped fields of their own record, but governance of the data — and of everyone else's — stays with the church.
definition.dc_zh: 教会端管理。工作人员和教友领袖持有权限访问并维护名单；成员可以自行编辑其自身记录的限定字段，但数据的治理——以及其他所有人的数据——仍由教会掌握。
definition.rules:
### Status is governed, not self-declared

Membership status changes are recorded by the church — through a class, a rite, a transfer, or an administrative action — not by the member clicking a button. The member may self-edit contact fields; the status belongs to the congregation's governance.

### Status drives visibility and eligibility

Directory inclusion, communication eligibility, and reporting categories typically depend on status. A visitor, an active member, and an inactive member appear differently (or not at all) in the directory and the lists built from the roll.

### The roll is the substrate

Other systems — giving, check-in, communication, scheduling — attribute their records to people on the roll and often sync from it. This single-record invariant is why standalone tools in the same market advertise their integration with the membership database, and why the roll can be sold as a product of its own.

### Removal is a status, not an erasure

Leaving the roll is recorded as a terminal status (transferred out, inactive, deceased) rather than as a deletion — the status model itself keeps the person on the roll, because pastoral records, letters of transfer, and historical reporting depend on the continuity of the record.

### Congregant data is sensitive by default

Visitation and counseling notes, health information, and directory visibility are privacy-controlled structures. Members commonly control whether they appear in the directory; children's information is handled with particular care.

### Attendance is a signal, not machinery

Recording that a person attended is a membership-health observation. The full machinery of check-in stations, security labels, and custody protocols belongs to the church-management-system type; here attendance stays light — a dated mark on the person.
definition.rules_zh:
### 状态是被管理的，而非自我声明的

会员状态变更是由教会记录的——通过一个课程、一个仪式、一个转介或一项管理操作——而不是由会员点击按钮。会员可以自行编辑联系信息字段；但状态属于会众的治理范畴。

### 状态驱动可见性和资格

目录收录、通信资格和报告类别通常依赖于状态。访客、活跃会员和非活跃会员在目录和基于名册构建的名单中呈现不同（或根本不出现）。

### 名册是基础

其他系统——捐赠、签到、通信、排班——将其记录归因于名册上的人员，并通常从中同步。这种单一记录的不变性，正是同一市场中的独立工具会宣传其与会员数据库集成的原因，也是名册本身可以作为产品出售的原因。

### 移除是一种状态，而非擦除

离开名册被记录为一种终结状态（转出、非活跃、已故），而不是删除——状态模型本身将人员保留在名册上，因为牧灵记录、转介信和历史报告都依赖于记录的连续性。

### 会众数据默认是敏感的

探访和辅导笔记、健康信息以及目录可见性都是受隐私控制的结构。会员通常控制是否在目录中显示；儿童信息的处理尤为谨慎。

### 出席是一个信号，而非机制

记录某人出席是对会员健康状况的一种观察。完整的签到站、安全标签和监护协议机制属于教会管理系统的类型；在这里，出席记录保持轻量
